name: og-29-endogenous-autocatalysis
title: Endogenous Autocatalysis
claim: Vent-fed chemistry, assembled from the study-28 atlas reactions under the study-27 interface feeds, either forms a genuinely balanced, mass-conserving autocatalytic cycle whose amplification beats a matched null with equal chemical input fluxes — or it does not, in which case the study names the specific missing precursor or rate-limiting mechanism. Spontaneous network amplification is a claim won against a null, never inferred from apparent growth.
question: Can vent-fed chemistry spontaneously form network amplification or self-maintaining cycles — genuine, balanced autocatalysis rather than accumulation driven by the input feed?
hypothesis: Given the 27 interface feeds and the 28 reaction set, stoichiometric autocatalysis detection plus kinetic simulation under dilution will reveal whether a self-amplifying cycle exists; if it does, its amplification and net carbon fixation exceed a matched null (identical input fluxes, autocatalytic topology removed) and persist above a critical dilution rate; if it does not, the analysis isolates the missing precursor or rate-limiting step.
objective: Assemble vent-fed reaction networks from the 27 and 28 handoff bundles, detect stoichiometric autocatalysis, simulate kinetics with dilution, and test any detected amplification against a matched null — reporting either genuine autocatalysis with its critical dilution, or a clean negative that names the gap.
proposed_mechanisms: network amplification / self-maintaining cycles seeded from atlas reactions
stoichiometric autocatalysis (a subnetwork that produces its own catalyst/seed)
dilution as the selective pressure separating true autocatalysis from feed-driven accumulation
proposed_models_methods: RDKit rule-generated reaction candidates + curated atlas alternatives [to-build: reaction-rule-generation / viva_reaction_atlas]
stoichiometric autocatalysis detection on the reaction network (algebraic, pre-kinetic)
COPASI/libRoadRunner kinetic simulation with dilution                 [in-workspace: viva_genesis.protometabolism]
discrete/stochastic kinetics where expected molecule counts make continuum concentrations unreliable (evidence standard
eQuilibrator ΔG screen so any detected cycle is thermodynamically allowed [exists: viva_equilibrator]
matched-null construction + PyMC/SALib sensitivity & identifiability   [partial: viva_genesis.uq]

model_approach.prose: Study 29 is the chemical-emergence test. It assumes no amplification; it consumes the 27 feeds and 28 reactions as given typed bundles, detects candidate autocatalytic cycles stoichiometrically (before any kinetics), then simulates them under dilution. The decisive control is the matched null — the same chemical input fluxes with the autocatalytic coupling removed — and only amplification that beats that null counts as autocatalysis. Low-count intermediates are simulated with discrete kinetics so a handful of molecules is never mistaken for a continuum concentration.

behavior_tests.name: stoichiometric-autocatalysis-detection
behavior_tests.description: Stoichiometric detection plus kinetic simulation either exhibit a balanced, mass-conserving autocatalytic cycle with measurable amplification and net carbon fixation, or they do not.

behavior_tests.name: autocatalysis-beats-matched-null
behavior_tests.description: Any detected amplification must exceed a matched null (identical chemical input fluxes, autocatalytic topology removed); amplification not separable from the null is reported as feed-driven accumulation, not autocatalysis. This is the Gate A null arm.

behavior_tests.name: critical-dilution-threshold
behavior_tests.description: The study reports the critical dilution rate above which any self-maintaining cycle collapses — its robustness envelope, not a single operating point.

measure.detail: autocatalytic gain vs. dilution rate; critical dilution at collapse

pass_if.detail: critical dilution rate reported (robustness envelope characterised)

behavior_tests.name: carbon-conservation-ledger
behavior_tests.description: Carbon, mass and charge close across the kinetic run with the 27 feeds as the only carbon/energy source; no untracked input.

measure.detail: C/mass/charge residuals across the kinetic run

behavior_tests.name: negative-result-isolates-gap
behavior_tests.description: If no genuine autocatalysis is found, the study isolates and names the missing precursor or rate-limiting mechanism — a clean negative is an accepted result that scopes downstream work.

measure.detail: on no-detection, the identified missing precursor / rate-limiting mechanism

pass_if.detail: balanced autocatalysis demonstrated OR a named missing precursor/mechanism

gate_A: Gate A (chemical emergence) = studies 27 + 28 + 29 passing together. Its acceptance REQUIRES that 29's detected autocatalysis beats the matched null with chemical input fluxes held equal; without the null-beating margin, Gate A does not pass regardless of raw amplification.
decision_test: Detect genuine balanced autocatalysis — a mass-conserving cycle whose amplification and net carbon fixation beat a matched null with equal input fluxes and persist above a critical dilution — OR identify the specific missing precursor/mechanism. A clean negative is a result; apparent growth that does not separate from the matched null is NOT autocatalysis and is reported as such (evidence standard #5, #8).

findings.statement: Study 29 receives the full 27→29 bundle — H2 + inorganic-carbon flux, pH, T, ionic activities, catalyst state and time-dependent feeds — as typed inputs, verified complete before any network is assembled.
Study 29 receives the full 28→29 bundle — canonical species, balanced stoichiometry, rate forms, parameter bounds and confidence tags — as the reaction set, verified complete.

Stoichiometric detection plus kinetic simulation either exhibit a balanced, mass-conserving autocatalytic cycle with measurable amplification and net carbon fixation, or they do not; the finding reports which, with the amplification factor and net fixation when positive.

Any detected amplification must exceed a matched null (identical chemical input fluxes, autocatalytic topology removed); amplification not separable from the null is reported as feed-driven accumulation, not autocatalysis. This is the Gate A null arm.
The study reports the critical dilution rate above which any self-maintaining cycle collapses — its robustness envelope, not a single operating point.
Carbon, mass and charge close across the kinetic run with the 27 feeds as the only carbon/energy source; no untracked input.

If no genuine autocatalysis is found, the study isolates and names the missing precursor or rate-limiting mechanism — a clean negative is an accepted result that scopes downstream work, not a failure to hide.

key_assumptions: Autocatalysis must be stoichiometrically balanced — an apparent cycle fed by an untracked source is rejected, not counted.
A matched non-concentrating / non-autocatalytic null is the control the favourable case must beat.
expert_questions: Is an honest negative (a named missing precursor/mechanism) an acceptable decision outcome here, or must a positive autocatalytic cycle be demonstrated to pass?
